inconsistencies: #36114 and #35358 solve the same problem (verifying the PSBT returned by an external signer before accepting it). Review #36114 first: it merges rather than replaces the signer's PSBT and also rejects unsafe sighash types; then decide whether #35358 still adds anything.

#34457 and #34533 both route wallet transaction rebroadcasts through private broadcast. #34457 is the superset (wallet sends plus rebroadcasts, plus Qt exception handling); review it first and treat #34533 as the narrower alternative.

Dependency chain: #32895 and #33033 -> #33034 -> #27865. #27865's 250x-500x balance speedup cannot merge before #33034, and #33034 states it depends on #32895 and #33033, so the two prerequisites were raised to P2 and placed ahead of it.
Dependency chain: #36230 -> #36133 (#36133 is based on #36230); review the descriptor-hash performance fix first.
Dependency chain: #35998 explicitly depends on #35752; the atomic encryption/commit work should be reviewed before the nodiscard sweep over WalletBatch callers.

Wallet database write-failure / corruption cluster that should be reviewed as a group for a consistent policy: #35752, #35998, #35492, #35760, #35440, #35989. Several change what happens on a failed or corrupt record, and they can contradict each other.

Multisig wizard project #35645 has four parallel prerequisites in this list: #35918, #36070, #36143, and (disputed) #36126. They are individually small; a single decision on the setup-flow API would unblock all of them.

Silent payments is one project split across #32966 (receiving) and #35302 (sending, based on #35301, tracked in #28536); receiving is additionally blocked on libsecp256k1 #1799. Band them together and sequence receiving first.

importdescriptors is touched by #31668 (skip rescan), #36236 (verify_balance), #35989 (range overflow crash), #36245 (top-up from range_start) and #35224 (error text). #36245 and #35989 are correctness fixes and should land before the feature options to avoid rebasing churn.

#35901's problem is confirmed but reviewers showed the author's prefix-rescan approach is incomplete and conflicts with #34681; it stays P1 because the missed-transaction/wrong-balance bug is category-critical regardless of which approach wins.
#19460 depends on the multiprocess branch (#10102/#29409) and is the base for #19461; it cannot be reviewed as a standalone wallet change.
result.notes: The category has a clear top tier of fund-safety and wallet-integrity bugs (missed transactions on rescan, SIGHASH_SINGLE signing, ignored database write failures, load-time assertion crash, truncated dumps), which I kept as P1. P2 is deliberately ordered correctness and performance first, then the large features (silent payments, codex32, external-signer flexibility), following the category rule that fund safety and migration/recovery correctness outrank new features. Three PRs were raised into P2 as stated prerequisites or memory-safety peers, and one fuzz target was lowered to P4 on reviewer-stated low efficacy; everything else keeps its original band.
